requirements.requirement: curl package is held at its current installed version on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline curl version 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8 captured, then `apt-mark hold curl` applied and confirmed present in `apt-mark showhold` output.

requirements.requirement: The hold causes curl to be excluded from a system update (package version unchanged after upgrade)
requirements.summary: A simulated `apt-get -s upgrade` showed curl kept back with no Inst line for curl, and a real `apt-get upgrade -y` was executed across the system; post-upgrade `dpkg -l curl` shows status 'hi' (hold+installed) still at the original version 8.5.0-2ubuntu10.8, directly demonstrating the hold survived a genuine system update.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 96c08b66... with curl held/unchanged; `shutdown -r now` issued and acknowledged before disconnect; connectivity poll timed out once then succeeded, consistent with a real reboot; post-restart boot_id 30c275ad... differs from baseline and matches the fixed after_executor snapshot; curl remained held at the same version post-restart, and package-health/failed-services checks in the fixed snapshots show no regressions.

overall_summary: The executor held curl at its current version via apt-mark hold and directly demonstrated—through both a simulated and a real full-system apt-get upgrade—that curl remained unchanged while other packages updated. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also completed with a clear pre/post boot-identity transition and recovered, unchanged curl-hold state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence.
limitations: The connection timeout during the reboot poll (cmd-4820c1fe71e64633) is expected behavior during a reboot rather than a failure, but relies on the subsequent successful poll and boot_id change as confirmation.

No explicit systemd service or data-integrity check beyond package-health/failed-services was captured post-restart, though this is a single-node package-management task with no stateful service to verify.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands are traceable to a material outcome: apt-mark hold (core task), apt-get update/simulated upgrade (read-only discovery), the real `apt-get upgrade -y` (bounded, system-wide package upgrade run specifically to prove the hold survives a genuine 'system update' as the task phrasing requires, not an unrelated experiment), and `shutdown -r now` (mandated restart-evidence protocol). The full-system upgrade is a broad mutation (kernel/initramfs regenerated, many packages updated) but it is directly motivated by validating the task's own requirement and left no abandoned residue; fixed snapshots after the run show no failed services and unchanged package-health status. No unnecessary or unreverted troubleshooting mutations were found in the timeline.
